symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Structural coefficient matrix in arbitrary common variable units, with \(B_{ji}\ne0\) for the edge \(i\to j\).

symbols.name: v
symbols.def: Innovation variances in the reference environment and the same arbitrary variable units as \(B\).

symbols.name: pi0
symbols.def: Any topological order of the true graph \(G\).

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: Generic first input to a canonical order predictor or deterministic perturbation comparison.

symbols.name: Cprime
symbols.def: Generic second input \(C'\) to the deterministic predictor perturbation comparison.

symbols.name: Bpi
symbols.def: \(B^{\pi}(C)\) is the sequential-regression coefficient matrix of a positive-definite correlation matrix \(C\) in order \(\pi\), as constructed below.

symbols.name: vpi
symbols.def: \(v^{\pi}(C)\) is the vector of sequential Schur residual variances of \(C\).

symbols.name: B0
symbols.def: True reference-standardized coefficient matrix \(B^0=B^{\pi_0}(R_0)\) for a true topological order \(\pi_0\in\operatorname{Top}(G)\).
symbols.role: Gauge-invariant coefficient target for support margins.

symbols.name: Phipi
symbols.def: \(\Phi_e^{\pi}(C;d)\) is the canonical correlation prediction constructed from \(C\), \(d\), and \(\pi\).

symbols.name: Omegapi
symbols.def: \(\Omega_e^{\pi}(C;d)=(I_p-B^{\pi}(C))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(v^{\pi}(C))D_e(I_p-B^{\pi}(C))^{-\mathsf T}\) is the unnormalized canonical covariance prediction.

symbols.name: F
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F(R,d)\) is the projective Cholesky support fiber constructed below.

symbols.name: PS
symbols.def: \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\) is pairwise projective separation of the normalized profile columns.

symbols.name: ThetaG
symbols.def: \(\Theta_G\) is the exact-support parameter stratum constructed below.

symbols.name: AlgFiber
symbols.def: \(\mathsf{FiberCert}\) is the exact all-order certificate-and-deduplication construction below.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: Independent site samples whose Gaussian copulas have latent correlations \(R_e\).

symbols.name: nstar
symbols.role: Effective sample size for Kendall concentration.

symbols.name: tauhat
symbols.def: \(\widehat\tau=(\widehat\tau_{e,ij})\) is the family of sample Kendall statistics.

symbols.name: m
symbols.def: Lower bound on normalized schedule entries.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: Upper bound on normalized schedule entries, with \(m\le M\).

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: Minimum nonzero entry of the true reference-standardized matrix \(B^0\).

symbols.name: eta
symbols.def: Generic minimum-eigenvalue argument for deterministic perturbation bounds.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: First edge coefficient in the tied-profile twin family.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Second edge coefficient in the tied-profile twin family.

symbols.name: u
symbols.def: First reference innovation variance in the tied-profile twin family.

symbols.name: w
symbols.def: Second reference innovation variance in the tied-profile twin family.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: Third reference innovation variance in the tied-profile twin family.

symbols.name: Ghat
symbols.def: \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha}\) is the graph confidence set constructed below.

symbols.name: Mpop
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d)\) is the maintained scale-erased excitation class constructed below.

symbols.name: Minf
symbols.def: \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d;\kappa,m,M,b,\delta)\) is the normalized margin class constructed below.

assumptions.condition: \(B_{jj}=0\) for every \(j\in V\), and \(B\) is strictly lower triangular after a simultaneous permutation of its rows and columns.

standard.name: Independent Gaussian innovations under diagonal noise interventions

assumptions.condition: \(d_{ej}>0\) is known for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(j\in V\), and \(d_{0j}=1\) for every \(j\in V\).

novel.justification: A calibrated experiment can record each innovation channel's variance multiplier relative to its own reference value. Absolute innovation scales and the units of observed variables need not be shared across sites.

assumptions.condition: \((X_{e\ell})_{\ell=1}^{n_e}\) are independent and identically distributed within each \(e\in\mathcal E\), independent across environments, and have continuous margins with Gaussian copula correlation \(R_e\).

standard.name: Gaussian copula sampling with continuous margins
Uniform positive-definiteness of a latent correlation matrix

assumptions.condition: \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(j\in V\).

novel.justification: Bounded reference-normalized excitation is imposed to keep perturbation constants uniform over calibrated experimental schedules. It is realistic when actuators operate inside a prespecified multiplicative range; bounded calibration error adds to the predictor discrepancy and consumes the same wrong-order score-separation budget through the predictor sensitivity modulus.

This is an explicit compactness restriction on the identified, dimensionless reference-standardized coefficient coordinates. It is invariant to every positive change of the unreleased variable units and excludes supports arbitrarily close to edge deletion.
This observable correlation-scale margin holds on compact subsets separated from the finite algebraic wrong-order loci and can be audited from the order predictors themselves.

definitions.name: Scale-erased excitation model class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d)=\{(B,v,(R_e)_{e\in\mathcal E}):Y_e=BY_e+\varepsilon_e,\ R_e=\operatorname{corr}((I_p-B)^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(v)D_e(I_p-B)^{-\mathsf T})\text{ for }e=0,\ldots,E-1\}\), with membership determined by the three listed member properties.

definitions.name: Pairwise projective separation
definitions.construction: \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\Longleftrightarrow[\forall i\ne j,\ \exists e\in\mathcal E:\ d_{ei}\ne d_{ej}]\). Because \(d_{0j}=1\), this is exactly projective distinctness of every two normalized schedule columns.

definitions.name: Exact-support parameter stratum
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_G=\{(B,v)\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}\times(0,\infty)^p:\operatorname{supp}(B)=G,\ B\text{ satisfies the acyclic linear-structure condition}\}\).

definitions.name: Canonical projective Cholesky predictor
definitions.construction: For \(S_j^{\pi}=\{i:\pi^{-1}(i)<\pi^{-1}(j)\}\), set \(B_{j,S_j^{\pi}}^{\pi}(C)=C[j,S_j^{\pi}]C[S_j^{\pi},S_j^{\pi}]^{-1}\), \(B_{j,V\setminus S_j^{\pi}}^{\pi}(C)=0\), and \(v_j^{\pi}(C)=1-C[j,S_j^{\pi}]C[S_j^{\pi},S_j^{\pi}]^{-1}C[S_j^{\pi},j]\). Put \(A^{\pi}(C)=(I_p-B^{\pi}(C))^{-1}\) and \(\Phi_e^{\pi}(C;d)=\operatorname{corr}(A^{\pi}(C)\operatorname{diag}(v^{\pi}(C))D_eA^{\pi}(C)^{\mathsf T})\).

definitions.name: Certificate-based exact all-order recovery
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf{FiberCert}(R,d)\) enumerates every \(\pi\in\mathfrak S_V\), forms \(B^{\pi}(R_0)\), \(v^{\pi}(R_0)\), and \(\Omega_e^{\pi}(R_0;d)\), and retains \(\operatorname{supp}(B^{\pi}(R_0))\) precisely when \(\Omega_{e,ii}^{\pi}(R_0;d)>0\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(i\in V\), and, for every \(e\in\mathcal E\) and \(i<j\), \((\Omega_{e,ij}^{\pi}(R_0;d))^2=R_{e,ij}^2\Omega_{e,ii}^{\pi}(R_0;d)\Omega_{e,jj}^{\pi}(R_0;d)\) and \(\Omega_{e,ij}^{\pi}(R_0;d)R_{e,ij}\ge0\). It deduplicates the retained labeled supports with a binary-support trie.

definitions.name: Conditional-pair peeling
definitions.construction: At state \(S\subseteq V\), maintain each conditional covariance by rank-one Schur updates and normalize it to \(R_e^{(S)}=\operatorname{corr}(R_e[V\setminus S,V\setminus S]-R_e[V\setminus S,S]R_e[S,S]^{-1}R_e[S,V\setminus S])\). Test every ordered pair \(i,j\in V\setminus S\) for \(R_{e,ij}^{(S)2}/(1-R_{e,ij}^{(S)2})=(d_{ei}/d_{ej})R_{0,ij}^{(S)2}/(1-R_{0,ij}^{(S)2})\) and a common correlation sign over all \(e\). If exactly one ordered pair passes, append its first vertex to \(S\); otherwise return \(\mathsf{FiberCert}(R,d)\). On completing an order, return its support only if the positivity, squared-cross-product, and sign checks in \(\mathsf{FiberCert}\) pass; otherwise return \(\mathsf{FiberCert}(R,d)\).

definitions.name: Gauge-invariant finite-sample margin class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d;\kappa,m,M,b,\delta)=\{(B,v,R)\in\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d):\lambda_{\min}(R_0)\ge\kappa,\ m\le d_{ej}\le M,\ \min_{B^0_{ji}\ne0}|B^0_{ji}|\ge b,\ \Delta(R,d,G)\ge\delta\}\), for \(e=0,\ldots,E-1\) and \(i,j=1,\ldots,p\).

definitions.name: Rank-summary graph confidence set
definitions.construction: Let \(K_B=8p^2\kappa^{-2}\), \(L=224(M/m)p^4\kappa^{-4}\), and \(T=(L+1)r\). If \(r\ge\kappa/(2p)\), \(b\le2K_Br\), or \(\lambda_{\min}(\widehat R_0)<\kappa/2\), set \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha}=\mathfrak G_V\). Otherwise set \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha}=\{\operatorname{supp}_{K_Br}(B^{\pi}(\widehat R_0)):Q_{\pi}(\widehat R,d)\le T,\ \pi\in\mathfrak S_V\}\), where \(\operatorname{supp}_{t}(C)=\{i\to j:|C_{ji}|>t\}\).

definitions.name: Projective-fragment quotient handle
definitions.construction: Use removed-set Schur states, equality tests between projective Cholesky fragments, and a canonical-augmentation parent rule as the starting mechanism for an exact-once sparse-fiber enumerator.

statements.statement: For every positive-definite correlation matrix \(C\) and order \(\pi\), \(C=(I_p-B^{\pi}(C))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(v^{\pi}(C))(I_p-B^{\pi}(C))^{-\mathsf T}\) is the unique unit-diagonal modified-Cholesky representation in order \(\pi\). For every member of \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d)\) and every \(\pi_0\in\operatorname{Top}(G)\), \(B^{\pi_0}(R_0)=B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\) and \(v^{\pi_0}(R_0)=\operatorname{diag}(H_0)^2\odot v\); hence \(B^0\) is independent of the chosen true topological order. The released family must equal \((\Phi_e^{\pi_0}(R_0;d))_{e\in\mathcal E}\). Under any positive common change of raw variable units, \(B\) and \(H_0\) transform contragrediently while \(R\), \(d\), \(B^0\), and every order score remain unchanged.
statements.justification: This lemma removes continuous scale search and identifies the unique gauge-invariant coefficient coordinates on which support separation can be imposed.
statements.gap: PetersBuhlmann2014EqualVariance, Theorem 1, uses recursive conditional variances under equal errors, while RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1, normalizes a joint diagonalizer of full covariance differences. Neither derives an order predictor or coefficient margin invariant to independently erased environment scales.
statements.consumer: A rank-only federation can validate a candidate causal order without reconstructing any site's marginal units.

statements.statement: Suppose \(d_{ei}=d_{ej}\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). For every \(\beta,\gamma\ne0\) and \(u,w,z>0\), the fork \(i\to j\), \(i\to k\), with coefficients \(\beta,\gamma\) and reference innovation variances \((u,w,z)\) in coordinate order \((i,j,k)\), has exactly the same covariance in every environment as the chain \(j\to i\to k\) with coefficients \(\beta u/(\beta^2u+w),\gamma\) and reference innovation variances \((uw/(\beta^2u+w),\beta^2u+w,z)\). Thus the two nonisomorphic exact supports form a positive-dimensional twin family. Setting \(\beta=\gamma=u=w=z=1\) gives the covariance block \(\begin{psmallmatrix}d_{ei}&d_{ei}&d_{ei}\\d_{ei}&2d_{ei}&d_{ei}\\d_{ei}&d_{ei}&d_{ei}+d_{ek}\end{psmallmatrix}\). For \(p=2\), deleting vertex \(k\) gives reverse one-edge twins; for \(p>3\), adjoining independent vertices embeds the family into the larger exact-support strata.
statements.justification: The positive fork--chain family proves necessity without zero innovations or vanished displayed edges.
statements.gap: RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Appendix A, perturbs covariance-difference diagonalizers; it does not exhibit nonisomorphic acyclic models whose full covariance families coincide under tied multiplicative profiles.
statements.consumer: Experimental designers receive an explicit impossibility certificate for any tied schedule pair.

statements.statement: The following are equivalent: \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\) holds; and, for every labeled DAG \(G\), every \((B,v)\in\Theta_G\) outside a proper real algebraic subset generates through \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d)\) a released family \(R\) satisfying \(\mathcal F(R,d)=\{G\}\). Under \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\), every nontopological order \(\pi\) violates at least one denominator-cleared correlation-matching polynomial that is not identically zero on \(\Theta_G\); hence the generically matching orders are exactly \(\operatorname{Top}(G)\), and each returns \(G\). If \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\) fails, the tied-profile constructions give a relatively open positive-parameter family in an exact-support stratum with a nonsingleton fiber.
statements.justification: This is the sharp universal generic excitation frontier after every marginal scale is erased.
statements.gap: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, identifies a causal graph from full environment densities through log-score and Hessian information using two auxiliary environments. GamellaEtAl2022GnIES, Theorem 6, characterizes sparsest full-distribution-equivalent graphs, RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Theorem 1 and equation (13), use pairwise noncollinearity of full covariance-difference profiles, and PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction, Sections 2--3, targets causal predictors through invariant conditional response laws. The present if-and-only-if result instead identifies the whole DAG from independently standardized correlation orbits and calibrated normalized schedules, permits one reference plus one auxiliary environment, and proves necessity with exact directed-support twins.
statements.consumer: BackShift-style and federated workflows obtain an exact test of whether sitewise standardization preserves universal generic DAG identification.

statements.statement: Assume \(\mathrm{PS}(d)\) and that \(G\) is complete relative to a total order \(\pi_0\). Outside a proper real algebraic subset of \(\Theta_G\), at every true ancestral prefix \(S=\{\pi_0(1),\ldots,\pi_0(s)\}\), the ordered pair \((\pi_0(s+1),\pi_0(s+2))\) satisfies the conditional-odds profile identities, while every other ordered pair fails at least one identity. Thus \(\mathsf{PairPeel}(R,d)\) selects the next true vertex at every stage and returns \(\{G\}\). Maintaining \(E\) conditional covariance matrices by one rank-one Schur update at each stage costs \(O(E(p-s)^2)\), testing all ordered pairs costs \(O(E(p-s)^2)\), and summation over \(s=0,\ldots,p-2\), together with the final positivity, squared-cross-product, and sign checks, costs \(O(Ep^3)\) exact-real arithmetic operations.
statements.justification: The theorem supplies the non-tautological local completeness argument and operation count behind cubic recovery on generic complete DAGs.
statements.gap: PetersBuhlmann2014EqualVariance, Theorem 1, and Park2020ConditionalVariance, Theorem 2, use scale-bearing conditional variances. The identities here use calibrated multiplier ratios and conditional correlations that survive independent site standardization.
statements.consumer: Dense systems can be recovered from calibrated rank-only environment summaries without factorial order traversal.

statements.statement: Let \(C,C'\) be correlation matrices with \(\lambda_{\min}(C)\wedge\lambda_{\min}(C')\ge\eta\) and \(\lVert C-C'\rVert_{\max}\le\epsilon\). Under \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\), simultaneously for every order \(\pi\), \(\lVert B^{\pi}(C)-B^{\pi}(C')\rVert_{\max}\le2p^2\eta^{-2}\epsilon\) and \(\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\lVert\Phi_e^{\pi}(C;d)-\Phi_e^{\pi}(C';d)\rVert_{\max}\le14(M/m)p^4\eta^{-4}\epsilon\).
statements.justification: This simultaneous modulus is the bridge from rank concentration to graph-valued inference over every candidate order.
statements.gap: MitraZhang2014RankCorrelation, Theorem 2, controls rank-correlation submatrices, and Afsari2008JDSensitivity studies diagonalizer sensitivity; neither propagates errors uniformly through all projective Cholesky predictors.
statements.consumer: Federated analysts obtain explicit penalties for weak correlation conditioning and dispersed normalized excitations.

statements.statement: Under the continuous Gaussian-copula sampling condition, \(\Pr(\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\lVert\widehat R_e-R_e\rVert_{\max}\le r)\ge1-\alpha\). For every law in \(\mathfrak M_{p,E}(d;\kappa,m,M,b,\delta)\), \(\Pr(G\in\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha})\ge1-\alpha\). If \(r<\kappa/(2p)\), \(b>2K_Br\), and \(\delta>2T\), then on the same simultaneous event \(\widehat{\mathcal G}_{\alpha}=\{G\}\). Here \(b\) is exclusively the minimum signal of \(B^0=B^{\pi_0}(R_0)\), so the threshold, fallback, coverage domain, and singleton conclusion are unchanged by arbitrary positive reference rescaling.
statements.justification: The theorem converts rank-only releases into an honest support confidence set with a measurable all-DAG fallback.
statements.gap: LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic, Theorem 4.2, gives the uniform sine-transformed Kendall correlation bound, while Theorem 4.3 transfers it to undirected precision procedures. WangKolarDrton2025ConfidenceOrderings, Theorem 1, gives asymptotic ordering-set validity for residual-bootstrap tests. Neither supplies finite-sample inversion of calibrated multi-environment projective scores or a gauge-invariant directed-support margin.
statements.consumer: FedCDH-style sites can send Kendall matrices and sample sizes while the coordinator reports all causal supports not ruled out at level \(\alpha\).

statements.statement: Can the projective-fragment quotient handle yield an exact-real algorithm that returns each support in \(\mathcal F(R,d)\) exactly once with runtime \(2^p\operatorname{poly}(p,E)+N_{\mathrm{out}}\operatorname{poly}(p,E)\), or with polynomial delay, for arbitrary sparse fibers, together with a matching family exhibiting factorial duplication under naive order traversal?
statements.justification: Sparse supports may have many topological orders representing one numerical continuation, so identification alone does not give output-sensitive computation.
statements.gap: WangEtAl2023EquivalenceEnumeration and WienobstEtAl2023MECEnumeration use graphical canonical augmentation, but no local congruence is known for equality of numerical projective Cholesky fragments.
statements.consumer: Exact confidence-set software could enumerate large sparse fibers without paying once per redundant topological order.

sampling_model.design: Each site receives a known positive innovation-variance schedule normalized coordinatewise to the reference environment, \(d_{0j}=1\), and releases only coordinate ranks or a Kendall matrix. Absolute innovation multipliers, when experimentally recorded, are merely one interpretation whose reference ratios produce \(d\); they are not maintained inputs.
sampling_model.units: Within environment \(e\), \(n_e\) observations are independent and identically distributed from one continuous-margin Gaussian copula, and samples are independent across environments.
sampling_model.treatment: Environment \(e\) changes reference innovation variance \(v_j\) to \(v_jd_{ej}\) while leaving the structural matrix invariant.
sampling_model.overlap: Population identification requires a distinct normalized profile for every vertex pair; uniform inference also requires \(m\le d_{ej}\le M\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Estimate \(R_e\) by the sine transform of the Kendall matrix; no marginal transformations, marginal variances, absolute excitation scales, or raw observations are pooled.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 identifies a normalized joint diagonalizer from full covariance differences under pairwise noncollinearity of shift profiles.
Theorem 6 characterizes the sparsest full-distribution-equivalent graphs under faithfulness, intervention heterogeneity, and model truthfulness.

Section 3, Theorem 1 identifies the causal graph from full environment densities through log-density Hessian differences under two auxiliary environments and pairwise distinct diagonal Hessian ratios.
Theorem 1 identifies a linear Gaussian DAG from one observational distribution under equal error variances.
Sections 2--3 retain predictor sets whose conditional response law is invariant across environments and provide confidence statements and sufficient identification conditions for causal predictors.
Theorem 2 gives sufficient forward or backward conditional-variance inequalities for identifying an additive-noise DAG from a full observational law.
Theorem 2 gives sufficient identifiability conditions for a nonlinear heteroscedastic-noise model with parent-dependent conditional variance.
Theorem 4.2 bounds the sine-transformed Kendall correlation estimator uniformly, and Theorem 4.3 transfers that bound to undirected precision procedures.
Theorem 2 controls spectral errors over collections of sine-transformed rank-correlation submatrices.
Theorem 1 establishes asymptotic validity of residual-bootstrap inversion for causal orderings.
Theorem 8 shows that communicated covariance tensors reproduce the paper's federated conditional-independence and independent-change statistics.
The article learns Gaussian latent-variable causal models under unknown additive interventions from full covariance information.

tldr: Known reference-normalized innovation multipliers can identify an invariant linear-Gaussian DAG even when every site releases only a Gaussian copula. The true structural coefficients are represented by the unit-free canonical matrix \(B^0=B^{\pi_0}(R_0)=H_0BH_0^{-1}\). Pairwise projective separation is the sharp universal generic frontier: wrong orders fail polynomial prediction identities, whereas tied profiles admit explicit reverse-edge and fork--chain twins. Exact all-order recovery uses signed squared-cross-product checks inside its construction, while the substantive conditional-pair theorem proves complete-DAG generic completeness and \(O(Ep^3)\) complexity. Uniform predictor bounds turn Kendall summaries into honest graph confidence sets under an explicit bounded normalized-excitation design regularity; the beta-min threshold, separation margin, and fallback are all expressed in reference-standardized units. Exact-once sparse-fiber enumeration remains open.

project_justification.gap: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, is the closest multiple-environment identifiability comparator, but it uses full environment densities through score and Hessian information and needs two auxiliary environments. BACKSHIFT uses covariance differences on a common numerical scale. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4, Theorem 6, uses full Gaussian environment distributions; the separate Journal of Machine Learning Research article by Taeb, Gamella, Heinze-Deml, and Bühlmann treats latent variables and unknown additive interventions. Invariant prediction tests stability of a response conditional law across environments, and conditional-variance identification uses scale-bearing observational quantities. None characterizes the full DAG fiber or honest support uncertainty from independently standardized correlations and a known normalized excitation schedule, including the reference-plus-one-environment frontier.
project_justification.niche: Acyclicity lets the reference correlation select one canonical standardized recursive model per order. The remaining correlations become predictions indexed only by the normalized schedule, so both identification and inference live on a diagonal-gauge quotient.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the universal generic if-and-only-if frontier and tied-profile necessity family, uses the reference-standardized coordinate \(B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\), gives a non-tautological conditional-pair completeness and cubic-complexity theorem for generic complete DAGs, and closes rank-summary inference under explicit gauge-invariant margins and bounded calibrated design profiles. Signed polynomial checks remain part of the exhaustive algorithm specification, not a separate contribution.

related_work: Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, is the closest multiple-environment pairwise-noise-ratio identifiability comparator. It observes full environment densities and extracts score and Hessian information, using two auxiliary environments to form two Hessian-difference groups whose diagonal ratio has distinct entries. The present observation regime releases only independently standardized correlation orbits with known normalized excitation profiles and proves a sharp reference-plus-one-environment frontier; Montagna's density-level theorem therefore informs but does not subsume the projective-copula result. RothenhauslerEtAl2015BackShift, Section 2.4, equation (10), Theorem 1, and Appendix A, is a related identification template but starts from covariance differences measured on one common scale. For any positive diagonal \(H_e\), \(\operatorname{corr}(H_e\Sigma_eH_e)=R_e\), while changing one diagonal entry of one \(H_e\) changes a covariance difference; therefore independently standardized correlations do not determine BACKSHIFT's input. This is an elementary observation about the observation regime, not a theorem contribution. PetersBuhlmann2014EqualVariance, Theorem 1, supplies a recursive triangular-factorization precedent. PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction, Sections 2--3, intersects predictor sets whose conditional response law remains invariant across environments and provides confidence statements for causal predictors. That intervention-invariance observation is different from observing only standardized joint correlations: the present target is the whole DAG, and its identifying variation is a known coordinatewise normalized noise-variance schedule rather than an invariant response regression. GamellaEtAl2022GnIES is the GnIES manuscript arXiv:2211.14897v4: equations (1)--(5) specify independent Gaussian innovations with environment-varying diagonal noise covariance, and Theorem 6 states that, under its assumptions, the intervention-equivalence class equals the sparsest distribution-equivalent graphs. Its full Gaussian environment distributions reveal scale-bearing variance interventions; independently standardized correlations retain only the calibrated ratios \(d\), so the canonical projective predictor is not a GnIES score specialization. TaebEtAl2024Latent is the distinct Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(293) article about latent-variable models with unknown additive interventions. Park2020ConditionalVariance, Theorem 2, uses marginal and conditional variances from a full observational law, while YinEtAl2024HNM, equation (5) and Theorem 2, uses parent-dependent conditional-variance functions in a nonlinear heteroscedastic-noise model. Those conditional-variance observation models are not available after unrelated site standardization; the present model instead uses cross-environment correlation predictions and known normalized excitation profiles. LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic, Theorem 4.2, supplies the uniform sine-transformed Kendall correlation bound, whereas Theorem 4.3 is only its plug-in transfer to undirected precision procedures. technical_internal_limitation: Generic identification is relative to each exact-support stratum and does not classify its real exceptional locus. Pairwise projective separation alone gives no uniform inference rate: coverage also uses correlation conditioning, the imposed bounded normalized-excitation design, reference-standardized beta-min, and wrong-order score separation. The cubic guarantee applies only to generic complete DAGs and uses exact-real rather than bit complexity. Unknown normalized schedules, cycles, latent confounding, varying mechanisms, singular correlations, zero innovation variances, unknown vertex correspondence, and discrete margins are outside the maintained model.
honest_scope: The supporting canonical-order lemma, universal generic frontier, tied-profile family, conditional-pair completeness and operation count, predictor perturbation bound, and finite-sample confidence theorem are proof obligations. The positivity, signed squared-cross-product, and deduplication steps specify exhaustive exact-real recovery and are not counted as theorem contributions; direct enumeration uses \(p!\) orders and \(O(Ep!p^3)\) arithmetic operations, excluding coefficient bit growth. Diagonal invariance of correlation and nonrecovery of covariance differences are elementary explanatory facts, not numbered claims. The normalized schedule \(d\), not any absolute multiplier array, is the maintained design input. Bounded schedule entries are an application-facing design regularity imposed for uniform constants, not a published standard condition. Bounded schedule-calibration error would add a predictor perturbation term that is subtracted from the wrong-order score-separation budget; the reference-standardized coefficient threshold is unchanged, and the stated theorem treats exact calibration. The confidence theorem uses only the unit-free matrix \(B^0\) for coefficient separation and returns all labeled DAGs whenever the same normalized thresholds cannot certify inversion. As supporting evidence, for \(p=3\), \(B_{21}=B_{31}=B_{32}=1\), \(v=(1,1,1)\), and \(d_1=(1,4,9)\), the unreleased representatives \(\Sigma_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&2\\1&2&3\\2&3&6\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(\Sigma_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1&2\\1&5&6\\2&6&17\end{psmallmatrix}\) induce the released correlations \(R_0=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/\sqrt2&\sqrt{2/3}\\1/\sqrt2&1&\sqrt3/2\\\sqrt{2/3}&\sqrt3/2&1\end{psmallmatrix}\) and \(R_1=\begin{psmallmatrix}1&1/\sqrt5&2/\sqrt{17}\\1/\sqrt5&1&6/\sqrt{85}\\2/\sqrt{17}&6/\sqrt{85}&1\end{psmallmatrix}\). Their first-pair shifted-odds comparisons are \(1/4,4/13,1/4,36/49,4/13,36/49\) against the six order predictions \(1/4,2/9,4,4/3,18,27/4\), excluding all five wrong orders exactly. This calculation is evidence, not a numbered claim. Two environments with pairwise distinct relative multipliers provide the required sanity reduction. Sparse output-sensitive exact-once enumeration is open.

literature_map: The kernel lies between covariance-shift identification, Gaussian noise-intervention equivalence, full-density multi-environment identification, intervention invariance, heteroscedastic conditional-variance identification, and rank-based causal inference. Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, equations (7)--(11), and Theorem 1 identify the graph from full environment densities via score and Hessian differences with two auxiliary environments; the present project instead has only independently standardized correlations and establishes a reference-plus-one-environment frontier. BACKSHIFT Section 2.4 and Theorem 1 use full covariance differences. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4 equations (1)--(5) and Theorem 6 use full Gaussian environment distributions with independent innovations; the Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(293) latent-variable paper is a distinct work. PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction, Sections 2--3, identifies causal predictors through invariant conditional response laws rather than a whole-DAG fiber from calibrated standardized correlations. Park2020ConditionalVariance and YinEtAl2024HNM identify from scale-bearing conditional variances, which independent standardization erases. LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic Theorem 4.2 gives the Kendall sine bound, whereas Theorem 4.3 is an undirected precision plug-in result. The present directed-support margin is explicitly imposed on \(B^0\), with VanDeGeerBuhlmann2013DAG cited only as support-recovery precedent. Afsari2008JDSensitivity motivates conditioning sensitivity but does not supply the bounded normalized-schedule assumption. The target remains exact acyclic support from a known normalized schedule and correlation-only releases.

novelty_justification: The closest multiple-environment comparator is Montagna2025InvariancePrinciple, Section 3, Theorem 1, which identifies the graph from full environment densities through score and Hessian information and requires two auxiliary environments. The present work observes only independently standardized correlation orbits and proves the reference-plus-one-environment frontier. BACKSHIFT Theorem 1 is another close template, but its covariance differences are not determined by independently gauged correlations. The new object is a canonical projective Cholesky fiber: each order yields a unique reference-standardized matrix \(B^{\pi}(R_0)\) and predicts every other correlation from only \(d\). Pairwise projective separation makes every nontopological match a nonzero polynomial, while tied profiles yield exact reverse-edge and positive fork--chain twins, producing a universal generic if-and-only-if frontier. GnIES arXiv:2211.14897v4, Theorem 6, is only an informed-by full-distribution comparator, the distinct TaebEtAl2024Latent paper is not conflated with it, and PetersEtAl2016InvariantPrediction targets invariant conditional response laws rather than this whole-DAG correlation quotient. Park2020ConditionalVariance and YinEtAl2024HNM require scale-bearing conditional variances and do not subsume calibrated correlation prediction. The positivity, signed squared-cross-product, and order-compatibility checks belong only to the exhaustive algorithm construction and are not claimed as a theorem contribution. The conditional-pair theorem contributes the independent local completeness proof and stagewise \(O(Ep^3)\) operation count. The inference layer treats bounded normalized excitation as a novel design regularity, consistently thresholds \(B^0=H_0BH_0^{-1}\), uses the same unit-free margin in its class, fallback, and singleton condition, and relies on LiuEtAl2012NPNskeptic Theorem 4.2 only for the Kendall correlation event.
